mainTopic: What a מבוי needs to be permitted by a לחי or קורה: the views of רב, שמואל and רבי יוחנן, the גזירה link to רבי שמעון's משנה, and the challenge to שמואל
overview: This amud begins by finishing רב's rule that a מבוי needs several houses and courtyards opening into it before a לחי or קורה can permit carrying. שמואל says one house and one courtyard are enough, and רבי יוחנן says even a חורבה (ruin) counts. רב יוסף explains to אביי that a ruin counts because it is fit to live in, but a vineyard path is not. רב הונא בר חיננא then shows that רבי יוחנן is consistent. He brings רבי שמעון's משנה that roofs, enclosures, and courtyards are one domain. רב rules like רבי שמעון only when no עירוב was made, because of a גזירה. שמואל and רבי יוחנן rule like רבי שמעון in every case. The גמרא infers that רבי יוחנן does not make such a גזירה, and that is why he permits the alleyway with a ruin. In a story, רבי אלעזר challenges שמואל with שמואל's own rule to follow the משנה's wording, and שמואל stays silent. The גמרא asks whether שמואל retracted, and it begins a proof from איבות בר איהי's alleyway that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב's requirement: houses and courtyards must open into the alleyway
steps.stepSummary: The end of רב's rule: a מבוי is only permitted by a לחי or קורה if houses and courtyards open into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...unless there are houses and courtyards opening into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement it started on the previous amud. רב said a מבוי cannot be fixed with a לחי or קורה unless houses and courtyards open into it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural words 'houses' and 'courtyards' mean there must be at least two courtyards, each with at least two houses. Without that, the area does not count as a real מבוי, so a לחי or קורה cannot permit carrying there.

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway that courtyards open into
A side post placed at the alleyway's entrance
A cross beam placed over the alleyway's entrance

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the strictest of the three opinions. The two opinions after it each lower the requirement step by step.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ בָּתִּים וַחֲצֵירוֹת פְּתוּחִין לְתוֹכוֹ.
phrases.english: unless there are houses and courtyards opening into it.
phrases.notes: Because 'houses' and 'courtyards' are plural, רב says you need at least two courtyards, each with at least two houses.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ בָּתִּים וַחֲצֵירוֹת פְּתוּחִין לְתוֹכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב's statement, which began earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מבוי needs multiple houses and multiple courtyards opening into it before a לחי or קורה can permit carrying.

steps.title: שמואל: one house and one courtyard are enough
steps.stepSummary: שמואל lowers the requirement to one house and one courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: Even one house and one courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב. He says even a single house and a single courtyard opening into the alleyway are enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב required several houses and several courtyards. שמואל says the smallest possible setup still makes the area a real מבוי, so a לחי or קורה can work there.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Even one house and one courtyard.
phrases.notes: Meaning one house with no courtyard of its own, plus one courtyard that has a house.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בַּיִת אֶחָד וְחָצֵר אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב and makes the requirement easier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One house and one courtyard opening into the alleyway are enough.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even a ruin counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says even a חורבה can count toward what a מבוי needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Even a ruin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן is even more lenient than שמואל. He says a ruined building, together with a courtyard that has a house, is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל needed an actual house. רבי יוחנן says even a broken-down structure can fill that spot. This leaves an open question: how far does this leniency go? The next step asks exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: A ruin; a destroyed or abandoned building

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels here. רב needs many houses and courtyards. שמואל needs one house and one courtyard. רבי יוחנן accepts even a ruin.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said: Even a ruin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes one step further than שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a ruin, together with a courtyard that has a house, is enough.

steps.title: אביי asks whether a vineyard path also counts
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף whether רבי יוחנן's leniency also covers a vineyard path.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Did רבי יוחנן say even a vineyard path?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי wants to know where רבי יוחנן's leniency stops. If a ruin counts, does a path through vineyards count too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a ruin and a vineyard path are places where nobody is currently living. אביי is testing whether 'not a real house' is good enough in general, or whether the ruin has some special quality.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁל כְּרָמִים?
phrases.english: Did Rabbi Yochanan say even a vineyard path?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁל כְּרָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רבי יוחנן's ruling reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יוחנן's leniency also include a vineyard path?

steps.title: רב יוסף: only a ruin, because it can be lived in
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that a ruin counts because it can serve as a home. A vineyard path cannot, so it does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי יוחנן said it only about a ruin, which is fit to live in. But a vineyard path, which is not fit to live in, does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי's question. The key factor is whether the place is fit to be lived in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruin can be rebuilt or used as a home, so it is still treated as a living space. A vineyard path is never a place where people live. That is why רבי יוחנן's leniency stops at the ruin.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to serve as a residence

steps.whatToRemember: The test is fitness to be lived in (ראוי לדירה). A ruin passes this test. A vineyard path fails it.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אֶלָּא בְּחוּרְבָּה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said it only about a ruin,
which is fit to be lived in.
But a vineyard path,
which is not fit to be lived in, does not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אֶלָּא בְּחוּרְבָּה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only a ruin counts, because it is fit to live in. A vineyard path does not count.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן follows his usual reasoning, based on רבי שמעון's משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא connects רבי יוחנן's view to רבי שמעון's משנה, which says roofs, enclosures, and courtyards are one domain for objects that started Shabbat there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חיננא said: רבי יוחנן is following his own reasoning. As we learned (רבי שמעון said): Roofs, enclosures, and courtyards are all one domain for objects that were inside them when שבת began, but not for objects that were inside the house when שבת began.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר חיננא shows that רבי יוחנן's ruling about the ruin fits a consistent pattern. He brings רבי שמעון's משנה as the background for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון treats roofs, enclosures, and courtyards as one shared domain for objects that were there when שבת began, but not for objects that started שבת inside a house. The link to רבי יוחנן's ruin is not about a ruin being an 'open area.' Steps 9–10 show the real link: רבי יוחנן makes no גזירה out of fear that people will carry objects into a forbidden area.

keyTerms.meaning: He is following his own consistent reasoning
As we learned in a משנה
Enclosed open areas outside the home
That 'rested' there, meaning they were there when שבת began

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not say that everything may be carried everywhere. The 'one domain' rule covers only objects that were in the courtyard, roof, or enclosure when שבת began. Objects that started שבת in a house are not included.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chinnana said:
And Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning,
as we learned in a Mishnah (Rabbi Shimon said):

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד גַּגּוֹת וְאֶחָד קַרְפֵּיפוֹת וְאֶחָד חֲצֵרוֹת —
phrases.english: Roofs, enclosures, and courtyards alike
are one domain
for objects that were inside them when Shabbat began,
but not for objects that were inside the house when Shabbat began.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining רבי יוחנן's ruling to showing where its reasoning comes from.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's leniency that even a ruin counts
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's משנה that roofs, enclosures, and courtyards are one domain

steps.title: רב rules like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב said: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling that רבי שמעון's view is the practical halacha. This sets up the limit that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns רבי שמעון's view from one opinion among several into practical law. The ruling is about to be narrowed in the next step.

phrases.english: And Rav said: The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the משנה just quoted.

steps.title: Only when they did not make an עירוב, because of a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון's leniency applies only when the courtyards made no עירוב. If they did make one, the Rabbis made a גזירה forbidding it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only where they did not make an עירוב. But if they made an עירוב, we decree against it, lest they come to take objects from the houses out to the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב limits his own ruling. The leniency only works when no עירוב was made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without an עירוב, nobody carries from their house into the courtyard, so there is no risk of mixing things up. With an עירוב, people do carry house objects into their courtyard. They might then carry those house objects from one courtyard to another, which is forbidden. To prevent that mistake, the Rabbis made a גזירה forbidding carrying between the areas in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects that belong in the houses

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, the הלכה follows רבי שמעון only when no עירוב was made. When an עירוב was made, a גזירה forbids it. The next step shows that שמואל and רבי יוחנן disagree.
steps.confusionAlert: This seems backwards: making an עירוב leads to a stricter result! The reason is that the עירוב lets house objects into the courtyard, and that creates the risk of mixing them up.

phrases.english: And this applies only where they did not make an eruv.
But if they made an eruv, we decree against it,
lest they come to take out
objects from the houses to the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּא שֶׁלֹּא עֵירְבוּ. אֲבָל עֵירְבוּ, גָּזְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב's ruling to the case where no עירוב was made.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון's 'one domain' leniency applies only without an עירוב. With an עירוב, a גזירה forbids it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון only when no עירוב was made. When an עירוב was made, we make a גזירה lest house objects be carried out to the courtyard.

steps.title: שמואל and רבי יוחנן rule like רבי שמעון in every case
steps.stepSummary: Unlike רב, שמואל and רבי יוחנן say the הלכה follows רבי שמעון whether or not the courtyards made an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: whether they made an עירוב or did not make an עירוב. And so too רבי יוחנן said: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון, whether they made an עירוב or did not make an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion that disagrees with רב's limit from the last step. שמואל and רבי יוחנן say רבי שמעון's leniency always applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said the rabbis made a גזירה (protective decree) once the courtyards made an עירוב. שמואל and רבי יוחנן do not accept that גזירה. For them, roofs, enclosures, and courtyards count as one domain in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: They made an עירוב (joined their courtyards together)
And so too said (another אמורא agrees)

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Whether they made an eruv or whether they did not make an eruv.
phrases.notes: In both cases the halacha follows רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: And so too Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon,
whether they made an eruv or whether they did not make an eruv.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: בֵּין עֵירְבוּ וּבֵין לֹא עֵירְבוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's limit in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון whether or not the courtyards made an עירוב.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן makes no decree, so the ruin is permitted too
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יוחנן's ruling, the גמרא infers that he does not make protective decrees. That explains why he permits carrying in a מבוי that has a ruin.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that we do not decree out of worry that people will carry house items into the courtyard. Here too, we do not decree out of worry that people will carry courtyard items into the ruin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רבי יוחנן's ruling. It ties that conclusion back to his lenient view about the ruin (חורבה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן allows carrying in the courtyard even after an עירוב, even though people might mix in items from the houses. So he is not worried about such mix-ups. The same reasoning lets him permit the מבוי with a ruin, even though someone might carry courtyard items into the ruin.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not make a protective decree
Lest he come to carry out

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's lenient ruling about the ruin fits his general view. He does not decree against carrying just because someone might carry into a forbidden area.

phrases.english: Apparently, we do not decree
lest he come to take out
objects of the houses to the courtyard;
here too, we do not decree
lest he come to take out
objects of the courtyard to the ruin.
phrases.notes: Even though the ruin isn't part of the עירוב, the rabbis didn't make a decree here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רבי יוחנן's ruling in Step 9 and completes the link proposed in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's leniency about a מבוי that contains a ruin.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling like רבי שמעון even when the courtyards made an עירוב.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר doubts a ruling reported in שמואל's name
steps.stepSummary: רב ברונא repeats a ruling of שמואל. רבי אלעזר is surprised, asks if שמואל really said it, and asks where שמואל is staying so he can check.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ברונא sat and taught this ruling. רבי אלעזר, a student of the academy, said to him: Did שמואל really say this?! He said: Yes. He said: Show me where he is staying. He showed him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. רבי אלעזר wants to check a ruling of שמואל at its source, which sets up a challenge to שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is that a מבוי with only one house and one courtyard can be permitted with a לחי or a קורה. רבי אלעזר finds this hard to believe. He wants to hear it from שמואל himself before he challenges it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'This ruling' (הא שמעתא) does NOT mean the ruling about רבי שמעון just quoted. It refers to an earlier ruling of שמואל on the daf: a מבוי with one house and one courtyard can be permitted with a לחי.

phrases.english: Rav Beruna sat
and was reciting this teaching.
phrases.notes: The teaching is שמואל's ruling that a מבוי with one house and one courtyard can be permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר בֵּי רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, a student of the academy, said to him:
Did Shmuel say this?!
He said to him: Yes.
He said to him: Show me his lodging.
He showed him.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב בְּרוֹנָא וְקָאָמַר לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי שמעון discussion and returns to שמואל's ruling from Step 2, that a מבוי with one house and one courtyard can be permitted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שמואל truly ruled that a מבוי with one house and one courtyard can be permitted.

steps.title: שמואל confirms he said it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר goes to שמואל and asks him directly. שמואל confirms the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before שמואל and said to him: Did the Master say this? He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל confirms the ruling is his. This sets up רבי אלעזר's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is no doubt that the ruling really comes from שמואל. That means any contradiction with his other statements is a real problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Master (a respectful way to address a rabbi)

phrases.english: He came before Shmuel,
and said to him: Did the Master say this?
He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the doubt raised in Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל confirms the ruling is his.

steps.title: Challenge from שמואל's own rule to follow the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר points out that שמואל himself said we follow the exact wording of the משנה. The משנה implies a מבוי needs more than one courtyard. שמואל is silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it the Master who said: in the laws of עירובין we only have the wording of our משנה, that a מבוי is to its courtyards like a courtyard is to its houses? He was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר challenges שמואל using שמואל's own principle. שמואל does not answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses plurals: 'courtyards' for a מבוי and 'houses' for a courtyard. Read exactly, this means a מבוי needs at least two courtyards. So a מבוי with only one courtyard should not be permitted with a לחי, which contradicts the ruling שמואל just confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it the Master who said (introduces a challenge from his own words)
According to the exact wording of our משנה
An alleyway that courtyards open into

phrases.english: But wasn't it the Master who said:
We have nothing in the laws of eruvin
except the wording of our Mishnah,
that an alleyway is to courtyards
phrases.notes: 'Courtyards' is plural, so it means at least two courtyards.

phrases.english: like a courtyard is to houses.
He was silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling שמואל confirmed in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a מבוי with one house and one courtyard can be permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's own principle is to follow the משנה's exact wording. That wording requires plural courtyards for a מבוי, so his ruling contradicts himself.

steps.title: Did שמואל accept the challenge?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל's silence means. Did he accept רבי אלעזר's challenge and retract, or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he accept it from him, or did he not accept it from him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what שמואל's silence means. It is setting up an attempted proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silence could mean שמואל agreed and took back his ruling. It could also mean he simply chose not to answer. This changes the practical הלכה for a מבוי with one courtyard.

phrases.english: Did he accept it from him,
or did he not accept it from him?

steps.triggerLanguage: קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ, אוֹ לָא קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the silence at the end of Step 13 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שמואל retracted his ruling after רבי אלעזר's challenge.

steps.title: A proof from איבות בר איהי's alleyway begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a story. איבות בר איהי lived in a מבוי with one house and one courtyard, put up a לחי, and שמואל permitted it. The proof continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: there was a certain מבוי that איבות בר איהי lived in. He made a לחי for it, and שמואל permitted it for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a proof from a real case to answer whether שמואל retracted. The story is not finished on this amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This מבוי had only one house and one courtyard, yet שמואל permitted it with a לחי. That suggests שמואל kept his lenient ruling. The next passage will show whether this proof holds.

keyTerms.meaning: A side post that permits carrying in a מבוי

steps.whyThisMatters: A rabbi's ruling in a real case (מעשה) carries weight for deciding the practical הלכה. So this story could settle whether שמואל held to his position.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
that a certain alleyway

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה דָּיַיר בֵּיהּ אַיְבוּת בַּר אִיהִי,
phrases.english: in which Ivut bar Ihi lived,
phrases.notes: It had only one house and one courtyard.

phrases.english: he made a side post for it,
and Shmuel permitted it for him,
phrases.notes: The story continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּהָהוּא מְבוֹאָה דַּהֲוָה דָּיַיר בֵּיהּ אַיְבוּת בַּר אִיהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל did not retract his ruling.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל permitting איבות בר איהי's single-courtyard מבוי with a לחי.
